description: Every command kraken-cli can run. `tool` names the MCP tool that calls it, `usage` gives the positional order, and `input_schema` is generated from the command's own Rust type, so it cannot drift from the arguments the command accepts. Its property names are the argument names a tool call takes. On the command line, the arguments `usage` lists are positional and every other property is a flag with hyphens for underscores (`min_fills` is `--min-fills`), except where `--help` spells it otherwise: `trade_type` and `ledger_type` are `--type`, `window` is `--for`, and `sessions` is `--session`. `constraints` states the cross-field requirements no schema keyword carries. Confirm any command with `dangerous: true`, and any `effect: local_or_live` one whose live argument is set (`--mode live`, `--real-account`): those reach the real account too. Route errors on the `error` field, never on message text (see agents/error-catalog.json).

commands.name: lab-compare
commands.description:
Compare every session of a frozen experiment side by side: each session re-scored from disk and judged against the sealed criteria.

Per-session verdicts are the only cross-session comparable numbers, because sessions cover different market windows. A session that cannot be scored appears as a named error column, never an omission, and `pass_count` counts only mechanically scored passing verdicts.

commands.name: lab-curve
commands.description:
The marked equity curve point by point — the full series `lab score` summarizes.

One point per valuation-changing instant with its timestamp, value and completeness flag, so a consumer can compute its own metrics (Sharpe, Sortino, rolling drawdown) without re-deriving the fold from the journal and tape. Refuses the same sessions `lab score` refuses: still recording, no final summary, a partial journal, or no account epoch.

session.description: Which session: `latest`, an ordinal (`s3`), or a label.

commands.name: lab-new
commands.description:
Pre-register an experiment: freeze a hypothesis and its success criteria (hash-sealed) before any session.

The seal is what makes a post-hoc goalpost move detectable; a frozen spec is immutable.

name.description: Experiment name (session charset; becomes session names).

strategy.description: The strategy under test, if one is named.

min_return_pct.description: Success: return of at least this percent.

max_drawdown_pct.description: Success: worst drop relative to its peak (max percentage drawdown) of at most this percent.

min_fills.description: Success: at least this many fills (guards a pass-by-not-trading).

sessions.description: Pre-register a session (repeatable, ordered): `live:<window>` or `replay:<ref>`. Replay tapes must exist and be finalized — their content hash is sealed with the spec.

commands.example: kraken lab new momentum-1 --hypothesis 'buying strength beats the tape' --min-return-pct 1 --min-fills 2 -o json

commands.name: lab-next
commands.description:
What the sealed session plan says to do now: the exact start command for the next run, the session still in progress, or `plan_complete` pointing at `kraken lab compare`.

Progress is re-derived from the sessions tree on every call; aborted sessions keep their ordinals and never count toward the plan. Refuses to hand out a replay session whose tape no longer matches its sealed content hash.

commands.name: lab-score
commands.description:
Score a stopped session: the explain-pnl waterfall plus mechanical metrics over the marked curve.

A source block naming the session's provenance (replay tape and speed, or live and symbols), the explain-pnl waterfall carried verbatim, and mechanical metrics — return, max drawdown, fees, friction, turnover, hit rate, profit factor, slippage sensitivity, trade counts — over the session's own recorded marks. Hit rate and profit factor grade closed FIFO round trips only and read null when no lot closed. Needs `kraken session stop` to have run first. With `--experiment`, judges the scorecard against a frozen experiment's criteria and adds a mechanical pass/fail verdict.

session.description: Which session: `latest`, an ordinal (`s3`), or a label.

experiment.description: Judge the scorecard against a frozen experiment's criteria; the output gains a mechanical pass/fail verdict.

commands.example: kraken lab score --session latest --experiment momentum-1 -o json

commands.name: lab-show
commands.description: Show a frozen experiment, verifying its seal.

commands.name: order-cancel
commands.description:
Cancel an open order by txid, userref, or client order ID.

Routed by workspace mode: inside a paper workspace it cancels on the workspace journal (a single txid only). Against the real account it sends one CancelOrder per transaction ID so each order's outcome is known — a sweep that only partly succeeds exits 1 with an `api` envelope carrying `cancelled` and `failed` lists, and only venue-confirmed cancels are recorded locally. Inside a live workspace it reconciles first and cancels only the order IDs that workspace recorded, never the account-wide CancelAll.

commands.name: order-cancel-all
commands.description:
Cancel all open orders.

Routed by workspace mode: inside a paper workspace it cancels on the workspace journal. Against the real account it sends Kraken's account-wide CancelAll and returns the `count` Kraken reports, then records every open order the local journal knows as cancelled. Inside a live workspace it reconciles first and cancels only the order IDs that workspace recorded, one CancelOrder each, never the account-wide CancelAll; a sweep that only partly succeeds exits 1 with an `api` envelope carrying `cancelled` and `failed` lists.

Derive a reusable recipe from a stopped session: an editable `recipe.json` plus a draft `SKILL.md` an agent can follow.

The recipe carries the driver skill, frozen strategy params, symbols, channels, sinks and provenance. Needs a paper workspace scope — a real-account session would bake real equity into a portable artifact. The recipe library is global, not workspace-scoped.

snapshot.description: Request an initial snapshot on subscribe, for the channels that carry one (`ticker`, `trade`, `book`, `ohlc`, `instrument`, `balances`); unset uses the server default. (`executions` snapshots via `--snap-trades`/`--snap-orders`.)

Sink targets: any combination of duckdb, jsonl, stdout (comma-separated).

items.description: A `--to` destination for a recorded stream: a durable backend, or a live stdout echo. duckdb: The file-based DuckDB tape (native columnar format; independent of `-o`).; jsonl: The dependency-free JSONL files (always JSON lines; independent of `-o`).; stdout: A live echo of the frames to stdout, rendered per `-o`/`--output`.

label.description: Human handle for this session, resolvable anywhere a session ref is (`--session <label>`). Must be unique within the scope.

strategy.description:
Identifier of the driving template (e.g. a recipe skill name); recorded in session.json.

The run hosts no strategy itself — this only labels the window so replay, explain-pnl, and the lab can attribute it to a hypothesis.

Opaque JSON parameters for the strategy, recorded verbatim in session.json.

Requires `--strategy`. A JSON object, e.g. `{"dollars_per_buy":100,"rounds":10}`.

from.description:
Replay a finalized recorded tape instead of streaming the live market.

Takes a ref from `kraken tape list` (`tape:<name>` or `session:s<n>`). The replayed frames are re-stamped to run wall time and re-recorded as the session's own tape, so trading, scoring, and explain work unchanged and stay REST-free.

speed.description: Playback speed for --from: tape seconds per wall second.

window.description: Auto-stop after this wall-clock window, then close the session (e.g. 20s, 5m, 1h, 24h). Without it, the session records until you `kraken session stop`. `kraken lab next` emits it for a plan's live entry.

commands.name: session-state-get
commands.description:
Read a session's state cell (unset reads as an empty cursor).

The durable cursor a long-running agent loop grounds on at each firing (round, legs done, zone, last action, note). A resumption aid, not history: deliberately outside the replay and scoring evidence, so it never appears in replay or `explain pnl`. An unset cell reads as an empty cursor with a null `updated_at`, never an error.

session.description: Which session: `latest`, an ordinal (`s3`), or a label.

commands.name: session-state-set
commands.description:
Replace the active session's state cell with the given fields.

Unset flags clear their cases. Refuses when no session is recording, and a mistyped field or zone refuses rather than steering the loop silently. This is a resumption cursor, not history — a transition worth a post-mortem belongs in `kraken session note`.

round.description: The last COMPLETED round; a firing acts as round+1 and writes it back.

legs_done.description: Pairs already executed in the round in flight (comma-separated).

last_action_at.description: Instant of the loop's last order (RFC 3339).

note.description: Free-text context for a human reading the artifact.

commands.example: kraken session state set --round 3 --zone above -o json

commands.name: session-stop
commands.description:
Stop a session's recorder, reconcile (real account), and close its window.

Against the real account it first reconciles the journal from venue history — fills the mirror missed enter under their venue txids, idempotently — and adopts the venue balance snapshot. Idempotent on an already-stopped session.

commands.description: Account balances, folded from the workspace journal.

commands.name: workspace-create
commands.description:
Create a workspace and seed its local capital journal.

Writes the contract (`workspace.json`) and seeds the journal with the capital epoch, in one step. Paper mode simulates fills locally and needs no credentials. Live mode allocates part of the configured Kraken account: it needs working credentials, checks the requested allocation against the real balance minus what other live workspaces already claim, and refuses an allocation the account cannot cover. Capital is fixed at create. Refuses the name `default`.

capital.description: Starting capital, or the live workspace's logical allocation.

currency.description: Capital currency, as the modern Kraken asset code (`BTC`, not `XBT`; `USD`, not `ZUSD`) — a workspace must key what its fills key.

mode.description: Required execution mode. paper: Simulated fills from the event-sourced engine, live market data.; live: Real orders attributed to this workspace through the configured account.

fee_rate.description: Fee rate as a decimal (default: 0.0026 = 0.26% Kraken Starter tier).

slippage_rate.description: Slippage rate as a decimal (default: 0.0 = no slippage simulation).

allow_pairs.description: Restrict trading to these pairs (comma-separated) — the paper analogue of API-key pair permissions. Omit = unrestricted; an empty value = deny-all.

commands.example: kraken workspace create btc-momentum --capital 10000 --mode paper -o json

commands.name: workspace-list
commands.description: List every account; `default` is the real Kraken account.

commands.name: workspace-promote
commands.description:
Evaluate the paper→live promotion checklist and switch the workspace to live execution on the real account when it passes.

The journal and history are preserved and the paper era is marked with a `fill_source_changed` event, so simulated history stays distinguishable from real history. Promotion also verifies that the account can cover the workspace's allocation, then requires explicit confirmation. Subsequent real spot orders use the normal configured credentials and are reconciled back into this workspace's ledger.

name.description: Workspace name (defaults to the active workspace).

commands.name: workspace-report
commands.description:
Account-first report of every session's outcome.

One row per session with opening and closing equity, P&L, fills, and the verdict taken verbatim from the scorecard anchor (never recomputed), plus the manual segment, reset epochs, venue drift, and digit-exact totals. A session that cannot be scored is a named error row, never an omission; a still-recording session is disclosed and excluded from every sum.

name.description: Workspace name (defaults to the active workspace).

commands.name: workspace-reset
commands.description:
Return a paper workspace to its starting capital.

A new reset epoch on the journal: history survives, but open orders and balances are superseded — destructive, and confirmed.

name.description: Workspace name (defaults to the active workspace).

capital.description: Re-parameterize on reset: new starting capital (updates the contract; omit to return to the created capital).

fee_rate.description: New fee rate as a decimal.
